'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Boko Haram insurgency]]
**[[Boko Haram]] militants raid and burn the village of Kadjigoroum, [[Chad]], killing nine civilians. [https://www.voanews.com/a/nine-chad-villagers-killed-in-jihadist-assault-/6240258.html (Voa News)]
*[[Korean conflict]]
**Addressing the [[United Nations General Assembly]], [[President of South Korea|South Korean president]] [[Moon Jae-in]] asks for a formal end to the decades-long conflict between the two Koreas. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/south-korean-leader-repeats-call-declaration-end-korean-war-2021-09-21/ (Reuters)]
*[[2019–2024 Sudanese transition to democracy]]
**[[Sudanese Armed Forces|Sudanese forces]] thwart a [[coup d'état|coup]] attempt against the ruling [[Sovereignty Council of Sudan|civilian-military government]] by supporters of former president [[Omar al-Bashir]] that began overnight. According to sources close to the government, [[interrogation]] of instigators would begin today. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/measures-being-taken-contain-failed-coup-attempt-sudan-official-source-2021-09-21/ (Reuters)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Governor of Michigan|Michigan Governor]] [[Gretchen Whitmer]] announces that [[Michigan]] will build an electrified road to charge wireless vehicles, becoming the first [[U.S. state]] to do so. [https://www.usatoday.com/story/money/cars/2021/09/21/michigan-first-wireless-electric-vehicle-charging-road/5804504001/ (''USA Today'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China]]
****[[Harbin]] bans visits to retirement homes, closes spas, cinemas and [[mahjong]] salons, reduces the capacity of tourist attractions by half, and suspends religious activities in order to reduce the spread of COVID-19 in poorly ventilated spaces after one community transmitted case was reported. [https://english.alarabiya.net/coronavirus/2021/09/21/Chinese-city-shuts-down-spas-mahjong-salons-after-positive-COVID-19-case (Al-Arabiya English)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****The number of recovered COVID-19 patients in [[Indonesia]] surpasses four million. [https://health.detik.com/berita-detikhealth/d-5733809/total-4-juta-orang-sembuh-covid-19-ri-tambah-3263-kasus-per-21-september (detikHealth)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****The number of adult population fully vaccinated against COVID-19 in [[Malaysia]] surpasses 80%. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/se-asia/malaysia-fully-vaccinated-80-of-adults-focus-turns-to-teens-and-covid-19-booster-shots (''The Straits Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore]]
****[[Singapore]] reports 1,178 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, which is the highest single-day total of new cases since April 2020. [https://www.businesstimes.com.sg/government-economy/three-more-covid-19-deaths-1178-new-covid-19-cases (''Business Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam]]
****[[Hanoi]] reopens non-essential services and removes travel permits for inner-city commuters. The city also allows food and drink establishments to reopen with takeaway only and a 9:00 p.m. closing time, due to a decline in the number of COVID-19 cases. [https://www.sify.com/news/non-essential-services-resume-in-hanoi-news-international-vjvkkfhfhcccd.html (Sify.com)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in New South Wales]]
*****Several [[Local government areas of New South Wales|regional area]]s of [[New South Wales]] enter a [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] after an increase in the number of [[COVID-19]] cases. At the same time, due to reaching statewide [[COVID-19 vaccination in Australia|vaccination]] targets, lockdown measures are relaxed slightly across New South Wales, with children under the age of 18 years old able to form a "friends bubble" with one other household. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2021/sep/21/nsw-covid-update-byron-bay-tweed-and-kempsey-in-lockdown-as-cases-and-deaths-rise (''The Guardian'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Solomon Islands]]
****The government announces that public servants will soon be a target of the "no jab, no job" policy and that they will have to either resign or receive half-pay if they refuse to receive a [[COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/451985/crunch-time-for-no-jab-no-job-policy-fast-approaching-in-solomon-islands (RNZ)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in California]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in the San Francisco Bay Area]]
*****[[San Francisco]] [[Mayor of San Francisco|Mayor]] [[London Breed]] announces that the [[San Francisco International Airport]] will mandate [[COVID-19 vaccine|COVID-19 vaccines]], making it the first U.S. airport to do so. [https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2021-09-21/san-francisco-airport-to-require-covid-vaccinations-for-workers (''Los Angeles Times'')]
*[[African Swine Fever]]
**[[Haiti]] reports the first outbreak of the African swine fever in 37 years when an operation in [[Anse-à-Pitre]] near border with the [[Dominican Republic]] suffered an outbreak that began on August 26. [https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/haiti-sees-first-african-swine-fever-outbreak-37-years-oie-2021-09-21/ (Reuters)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Australia–European Union relations]], [[Australia–France relations]]
**[[President of the European Commission]] [[Ursula von der Leyen]] suspends negotiations for a [[free trade]] agreement with [[Australia]] over Australia's recent cancellation of a submarine contract with [[France]], demanding that Australia must apologise to France before the agreement can continue. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2021/sep/21/aukus-row-european-union-demands-apology-from-australia-over-frances-treatment-before-trade-talks (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Foreign relations of Argentina]]
**[[Argentine President]] [[Alberto Fernández]] asks [[Iran]] to "cooperate with the [[Judiciary of Argentina|Argentine justice]]" regarding an investigation into the 1994 [[AMIA bombing]] in [[Buenos Aires]] and demands that countries where wanted [[Government of Iran|Iranian officials]] are residing should comply with its [[Interpol]] red notices. [https://www.infobae.com/politica/2021/09/21/ante-la-onu-alberto-fernandez-critico-al-fmi-y-dijo-que-argentina-fue-sometida-a-un-deudicidio/ (''Infobae'')]
*[[Recognition of the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan]], [[Foreign relations of Afghanistan]]
**In a letter to the [[United Nations Secretary-General]], the [[Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan]]'s [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Afghanistan)|Ministry of Foreign Affairs]] requests representation at the [[seventy-sixth session of the United Nations General Assembly]]. The Emirate's Foreign Minister Ameer Khan Muttaqi also requests that [[Permanent Representative of Afghanistan to the United Nations]] Ghulam Isaczai be replaced by Mohammad Suhail Shasheen. The Taliban also note that former [[President of Afghanistan|President]] [[Ashraf Ghani]] had been "ousted and [countries across the world] no longer recognize him as president." [https://www.cnn.com/2021/09/21/world/taliban-unga-intl/index.html (CNN)]
*[[Russia–United_Kingdom relations]]
**[[British police]] announce a third [[Russia|Russian]] had been charged [[Trial in absentia|in absentia]] with the 2018 [[Novichok_agent|Novichok]] murder attempt on former [[double agent]] [[Sergei Skripal]], saying they could also now confirm the three suspects were [[Federal Security Service|military intelligence operatives]]. [https://www.straitstimes.com/world/europe/the-third-man-uk-charges-another-russian-for-nerve-attack-on-double-agent (Straits Times)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Death of Gabby Petito]]
**A [[coroner]] in [[Teton County, Wyoming]], confirms that the remains found on September 19 were that of Petito, who disappeared from [[Grand Teton National Park]] on August 27, and rules her death a [[homicide]]. [https://www.todayonline.com/world/missing-us-woman-gabby-petito-confirmed-dead-homicide-fbi (AFP via ''Today'')]
*The [[European Court of Human Rights]] rules that agents acting on behalf of the [[Russian government]] were responsible for the fatal [[poisoning of Alexander Litvinenko]] in 2006. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-58637572 (BBC News)]
*The [[Court of Justice of the European Union]] imposes a daily fine of [[Euro|€]]500,000 (2.31M [[Polish zloty|zł]]) on [[Poland]] for its refusal to close the [[Turów Coal Mine]], which was declared illegal by a [[temporary injunction]] from the court in May. [https://www.cbs42.com/news/international/eu-court-fines-poland-500000-euros-daily-until-mine-closes/ (WIAT-TV)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[COVID-19 protests in Australia]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Victoria]]
**[[Victoria (Australia)|Victorian]] [[Premier of Victoria|Premier]] [[Daniel Andrews]] announces a two-week suspension of construction work in the state after yesterday's riot at the [[Construction, Forestry, Maritime, Mining and Energy Union]] (CFMEU) office. Rioters claimed that they were construction workers, although CFMEU officials and others claim that there were few construction workers present. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-09-21/victoria-construction-industry-shutdown-melbourne-protest-police/100478450 (ABC News Australia)]
**Protesters return to the [[Melbourne CBD]] for the second consecutive day, assaulting journalists and blocking the [[West Gate Freeway]]. [[Riot police]] responded with rubber bullet rounds. [https://www.nzherald.co.nz/world/covid-19-coronavirus-australia-melbourne-erupts-in-violent-anti-lockdown-protests-for-second-day/6IW53HVDEJIVHK5LBYX3VMYUSE/ (''New Zealand Herald'')]
*[[Women's rights in Afghanistan]]
**[[Taliban]] spokesperson [[Zabihullah Mujahid]] says that girls will return to school soon, adding that "We are finalizing things{{nbsp}}... it will happen as soon as possible". The announcement came as the Taliban banned girls from grades 6 to 12 from attending school, to which Mujahid said that this was only "temporary" and that new announcements would be made soon. [https://www.dw.com/en/afghanistan-girls-could-return-to-school-soon-says-taliban/a-59248723 (Deutsche Welle)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2022 FIFA World Cup qualification]], [[Racism in association football]]
**[[FIFA]] sanctions the [[Hungarian Football Federation]] with a [[US$]]216,000 fine and orders the [[Hungary national football team|Hungarian national team]] to play their next two [[2022 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA Group I|World Cup qualification]] [[Puskás Aréna|home]] matches [[Behind closed doors (sport)|behind closed doors]], following incidents of racist behavior among their fans during a match against [[England national football team|England]] on September 2. [https://edition.cnn.com/2021/09/21/football/hungary-stadium-ban-fine-england-racist-spt-intl/index.html (CNN)]
